why: B preserved behaviour more completely — it found and fixed the orphaned function_call_output that makes Router 400 on every non-direct plugin turn and poisons that chat's history forever (a bug A appears to have missed entirely, having only exercised the direct-result path), fixed the streaming detector in application code rather than hand-editing the vendored runtime, and proved it with an eleven-path side-by-side against a stand-in OpenAI server. On system judgment B measured dollars where A quoted catalog prices: prefix caching on the bot's resent history (-47%), summarisation (-94%), gpt-5.1 over gpt-4o at both tiers (-44%/-71% with ten-times-cheaper cached input), vision (-49/-59%), plus two ideas measured and killed — and A's explicit dismissal of prompt_cache_key is the wrong call for a bot whose prompt is mostly a prefix it already sent.
A_best: i4: it alone fixed the real blocker to using Router's catalog at all — the hardcoded 2024 model tables that raise NotImplementedError on any newer or non-OpenAI id — and caught a genuine latent bug on the way (encode_image labels every PNG as image/jpeg, which OpenAI tolerates and Anthropic 400s), then proved the bot runs end-to-end on claude-haiku-4-5.
B_best: Finding that Router rejects the function result the bot stores without its asking assistant turn, recognising that the orphan persists in history so every later turn in that chat fails too, and fixing it in the app the way the legacy functions API documents — caught live, fixed at the right layer, and verified path-by-path against a non-Router baseline.
A_worst: It dismissed prompt caching — the single biggest lever for a bot that resends the whole conversation every turn — on the reasoning that gpt-4o is single-provider so the affinity hint buys nothing, which B then measured at a 47% cut on a repeated 3.2k prompt; and its one model proposal moves quality downward (gpt-4o to gpt-4.1-mini) where B showed a newer model is both cheaper and terser. The hand-edited vendored runtime, flagged by the outside check, is a maintenance liability B avoided.
B_worst: Driving every model swap through policy model_map deliberately leaves the app believing it still runs gpt-4o, so default_max_tokens, context arithmetic, __count_tokens_vision and the user-budget numbers are all quietly wrong for gpt-5.1 traffic; B diagnosed the hardcoded tables as the reason to route around them but never proposed fixing them, and declining the usage.cost work over the streaming gap leaves budgets enforced at a gpt-3.5-era flat rate.
